_readme: Human participants in the study, transcribed from public posts.
This is a RESEARCH record, not a betting ledger. Everything here was said in
public, by someone who chose to say it, and is reproduced as they wrote it.
Nothing is paraphrased and nothing is tidied: "guy's inevitable" sits next to
"home form + set pieces should deliver" because the difference between a
feeling and a forecast is itself a finding.
Two states a participant can be in, and the page must never blur them:
- 'stated': they gave a prediction and a reason publicly. Nothing on chain.
- 'onchain': we helped them place it, and 'wallet' + 'fill' are filled in.
Only mark someone 'onchain' with their explicit agreement and their own
wallet. The handle is theirs; the money must be too.
context records what each person was replying to, because a prediction made
with the market price visible is a different thing from one made blind.

_fields.handle: X handle including the @, exactly as posted
_fields.displayName: as shown on X; may be empty
_fields.avatarUrl: X profile picture, resolved through unavatar.io by handle since the X API is not available to us. If the lookup fails the page falls back to initials, so a dead URL is cosmetically harmless.
_fields.url: link to the post, so a reader can check it
_fields.wallet: only when status is onchain and it is their own wallet
_fields.context: the gameweek, and the fact that pool prices were visible when they called it

predictions.reasoning: their words, verbatim. Trimmed only for length, never rewritten
predictions.probability: 0-1, ONLY if they actually gave a number. None of GW6's callers did, which is recorded as null rather than invented
predictions.confidence: high | medium | low | null -- and this is OUR reading of their wording, not something they said. Treated as a note, never as data

fill.signature: the on-chain transaction, once it exists
fill.helpedBy: who onboarded them, so the assistance is on the record
fill.stakeSource: us | them -- CRITICAL for interpretation. A call backed by our money and one backed by theirs are not the same evidence, and GW6 is all our money

_gw6_summary.observation: Every human call was YES. The five models placed ten positions and nine of them were NO. On Haaland and Saka the two groups are on OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE SAME PARIMUTUEL POOL, so the winning side is paid out of the losing side's stake. This is a literal head-to-head, not a comparison we tabulate ourselves.
_gw6_summary.caveat: Staked by us, not by them. A forecast with no cost behind it is weaker evidence than one with money on it, and the write-up has to say so.
